recent_posts.title: How We Built the AWS Data & Analytics Platform (Part 1)
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of building a scalable AWS-based data platform for an Australian beverage company handling diverse data sources including SAP systems, third-party vendors, and static files. The architecture uses AWS Step Functions to orchestrate three independent state machines for ingestion, processing, and loading data, with AWS Glue for ETL operations and Redshift for warehousing. Key design decisions include separating concerns across state machines, treating metadata capture as first-class, and leveraging visual orchestration for better troubleshooting.

recent_posts.title: Delta Live Pipelines Explained: Concepts to Implementation
recent_posts.summary: Delta Live Pipelines (DLT) simplify data engineering by automating infrastructure management, data quality checks, and monitoring while allowing developers to focus on transformation logic using SQL or Python. The framework supports both streaming and batch workloads through a declarative approach, handling common tasks like incremental data loading and SCD model creation. DLT pipelines can be created via code or Databricks UI, implementing medallion architecture patterns with built-in features for data lineage, quality reporting, and performance optimization.

recent_posts.title: Optimizing Spark configuration for small dataset processing
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to configure Apache Spark for processing very small datasets (100KB) by optimizing settings like using local mode, reducing shuffle partitions from 200 to 1-10, disabling Spark UI, and limiting executor resources. The author implemented these optimizations in Spark Playground, an online PySpark compiler running on AWS Lambda with Docker containers, achieving ~1 second average execution time for small data processing tasks.

recent_posts.title: Data contracts prevent pipeline breakages through schema agreements
recent_posts.summary: Data contracts act as agreements between data producers and consumers, defining schema structure, field types, and update frequencies to prevent pipeline breakages. They help teams avoid dashboard failures caused by unexpected schema changes like column renames or type modifications. Implementation can start simple with documentation in Git repositories and pull request reviews, gradually incorporating tools like dbt or specialized contract management systems. The approach reduces firefighting, improves team coordination, and builds stakeholder trust in data reliability.

recent_posts.title: Managing secrets in Databricks using CLI commands
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to managing secrets in Databricks using the CLI, covering installation, authentication methods (Personal Access Token vs User-to-Machine), creating secret scopes, adding secrets, managing access control lists, and retrieving secrets in notebooks. The tutorial includes practical examples for storing JSON credentials and emphasizes security best practices while recommending enterprise-grade solutions like AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault for production environments.

recent_posts.title: How I Built a Reddit Data Pipeline
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide to building an end-to-end data pipeline that extracts Reddit data, transforms it using AWS Glue, and stores it in S3 for querying with Athena and Redshift Spectrum. The tutorial covers environment setup with Docker and Airflow, infrastructure provisioning using Terraform, and implementing ETL workflows with proper orchestration. Key components include Reddit API integration, AWS services configuration (S3, Glue, Athena, Redshift), and DAG development for automated data processing.

recent_posts.title: SQL Server Gets a Python Power Boost: Exploring the Latest mssql-python Driver
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft released mssql-python v0.6.0, a modern native driver for SQL Server connectivity in Python. The driver replaces aging solutions like pyodbc and pymssql with features including cross-platform support (Windows and macOS, Linux coming soon), built-in connection pooling, Entra ID authentication, DB-API v2.0 compliance, and enhanced security with encrypted connections by default. Key improvements include named tuple row results, better error handling, Python 3.13.5 compatibility, and sensitive data masking in logs. The driver supports modern authentication methods including managed identity and Windows Integrated Authentication, with future plans for asyncio support and bulk copy API.

recent_posts.title: What Is Database Indexing? A Simple Guide for New Developers -Part 1
recent_posts.summary: Database indexing is a crucial optimization technique that helps avoid full table scans by creating organized structures that point directly to relevant data. Without indexes, queries must scan every row, leading to poor performance as data grows. The guide introduces two main types: ordered indices (using B+ trees) and hash indices. Key considerations for choosing indexing strategies include query patterns, performance requirements, data modification frequency, and storage constraints. The article sets up a foundation for understanding how indexes balance speed, storage, and data change frequency.

recent_posts.title: My Walmart Data Engineer III Interview Experience: Rounds, Questions & Tips
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of Walmart's Data Engineer III interview process, covering four rounds including technical SQL and DSA questions, Spark internals discussion, project deep-dives, and behavioral interviews. The candidate shares specific questions asked, preparation resources like LeetCode and StratasScratch, and optimization techniques that were tested. Key focus areas included SQL window functions, Spark memory management, data skew handling, and using the STAR method for behavioral questions.

recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive guide for becoming a data engineer in 2025, covering essential skills like SQL, Python, and data modeling, along with big data technologies like Apache Spark and cloud platforms. The roadmap emphasizes free learning resources and practical experience, highlighting that mastering core principles enables quick adaptation to new tools in the rapidly evolving data engineering landscape.
